initial.kalk:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: continuous educational ultrasound anatomy painting for a medical case reader.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and the SOLE geometric authority: the original clinical ultrasound. Input image 2 is SUPPORTING MATERIAL STYLE ONLY, and contains geometric drift which must NOT be copied.
Primary request: paint every visible tissue continuously over image 1 with the material language of image 2, retaining image 1's EXACT tissue silhouettes and spatial positions.
Composition: full 1280×960 canvas corresponding to image 1, same 4:3 aspect ratio. Preserve its black margins, scan field left edge x108, right edge x1171, upper scan boundary y111, scan depth and lower fade. Do not crop, zoom, pan, recenter, stretch only the anatomy, or enlarge the painted scan relative to image 1. Keep both the original acromion shape and the original humeral cortex curvature. Do not borrow bone/tendon positions from image 2.
Materials: fine organically curving brick-red deltoid fascicles, delicate ivory intramuscular fascia, golden lobular subcutaneous fat, ivory longitudinal tendon fibers, thin cream cortex, small irregular tan trabeculae fading softly into black depth. Deep shadows fade to black. Follow every visible fascial plane and fiber direction. No rigid straight fiber grids, triangles, seams, repeated tiles or muscle islands.
Text: NONE. Replace the acquisition header above y68 with solid black. Do not add labels, names, timestamps, arrows, outlines, legend, watermark or ultrasound controls. Existing black margin may remain black.
Constraints: clinical grayscale source is immutable reference; this is an explanatory color painting, not a diagnostic alteration. No extra lesions, bone, fluid collections or anatomy. The original scan geometry must remain traceable pixel for pixel after one uniform whole-canvas placement.
Affected-side specifics: preserve the original two irregular calcification masses and the intervening/adjacent tendon defect at their exact original locations. Existing fixed findings will point to central calcification (617,366), right calcification (916,367), and dark tendon defect (863,407) on a1280×960 canvas; the painting must align to these points rather than moving these points. Preserve the irregular bright calcification silhouettes, not just their centers. The humeral cortex apex remains approximately (800,448); left rising cortex approximately(430,610), right cortex approximately(1170,434). Preserve the separate acromion near left(175,280) without filling the intervening tendon or defect with bone. Dark navy may describe the existing dark defect only, using its original silhouette. Do not enlarge calcification or make new rupture gaps.
